title: Per-request compilation stays within 300 ms at p95, under a pinned protocol
statement: The 95th-percentile server-side time to compile and render the largest stage document in the project is at or below 300 ms, measured under this protocol. ENVIRONMENT: the reference host, with its OS, Node version, Next.js version and CPU model recorded alongside the result; no other significant load. DOCUMENT: the largest stage document by byte count at the time of evaluation, named in the result. TIMING BOUNDARY: from the moment the request handler begins the planning-content read to the moment the rendered document markup is complete, measured server-side; network and client time are excluded. WARM-UP: 10 requests are issued and discarded before measurement begins. SAMPLE: the next 50 consecutive requests, issued one at a time with no concurrency, are the measured set. VERIFICATION: each of the 50 must be shown to have actually compiled — a counter incremented per compile, or an equivalent observation, reported with the result. A run in which any measured request did not compile is VOID, not a pass.
notes: ⚠️ THE 300 ms IS A TARGET, NOT A MEASUREMENT, and saying so is the point: DEC-0020 recorded this cost as explicitly unmeasured. If the first evaluation misses it by a wide margin the answer is not to relax the number — it is DEC-0020's own second alternative, plain markdown for stage documents. Recorded as a number rather than 'acceptable' so the criterion stays pass/fail. ⚠️ AMENDED 2026-08-27 WITH A PROTOCOL, because the number alone was not a test. A budget with no pinned environment, no timing boundary and no warm-up treatment produces a figure nobody can reproduce or dispute, and 'p95 under 300 ms' would have been satisfiable by measuring the wrong thing on an unstated machine. ⚠️ THE VERIFICATION CLAUSE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST, and it is not routine hygiene. Without it the easiest way to pass is to cache the compiled document — which would report excellent numbers while measuring nothing, and would ALSO violate DEC-0020's request-time requirement and AST-0030's finding underneath it. A void run is not a failure and must not be recorded as one; it means the instrument was wrong, which is a different problem from the budget being missed. ⚠️ The 300 ms is still a TARGET rather than a measurement, and DEC-0020's third obligation stands: if the first valid run misses it by a wide margin the answer is that decision's own second alternative, plain markdown for stage documents — not a larger number. ⚠️ EVALUATED 2026-08-28 (EVD-0071): FAIL, and the reason is not the compiler. Six valid runs, three at 245-254 ms and three at 315-375 ms against the 300 ms budget. A criterion stated as a p95 ceiling is not met when half the valid measurements are above it, so this is `fail` rather than a pass with a caveat — but it is also NOT the failure this criterion anticipated. ⚠️ THE FALLBACK CLAUSE IS AIMED AT THE WRONG COST. MDX compilation measured 15-29 ms p95, 4-12% of the span; the planning-content read measured 234-359 ms. Applying DEC-0020's second alternative would surrender the restricted-MDX contract to remove roughly 20 ms and would still miss the budget. That clause was written when the cost was unmeasured; it now is, and it is somewhere else. ⚠️ THE PROTOCOL ITSELF NEEDS ONE MORE PIN. It fixes the host, document, warm-up, sample and timing boundary, but 'no other significant load' is not enforceable, and the read is I/O and validation heavy enough that ambient load moves the p95 by 50%. A protocol whose verdict flips between identical runs cannot settle a pass/fail question, whatever the number is. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-28: the 234-359 ms span was attributed here to reading all 253 artifacts per request. It is not. `readStageDocument` awaits `connection()` and reads the nine stage documents only — `lintProject` is not on its path. What inside that span costs the time is an open question, not a known cost. ⚠️ SUPERSEDED 2026-08-28 BY ACC-0037, WITH THE FAILURE LEFT STANDING. The outcome remains `fail` and this record remains readable: the budget was missed and that is history now, not a tick that was quietly flipped. What changed is the question being asked. This criterion bounded read-plus-compile, and the measurement showed the read dominates and the compiler does not, so ACC-0037 bounds the compile alone and QST-0025 carries the read as an open question. DEC-0025 records why the plain-Markdown fallback did not fire. ⚠️ THE SUCCESSOR IS NOT THIS ONE RELABELLED. Superseding a failed criterion with a wider version of the same claim would be editing the failure rather than answering it; the successor measures a different, narrower thing, and the part it dropped is carried by a question rather than dropped.
